Figure 1 : Self-Rewarding Language Models. Our self-alignment method consists of two steps: (i) Self-Instruction creation : newly created prompts are used to generate candidate responses from model M t subscript 𝑀 𝑡 M_{t} , which also predicts its own rewards via LLM-as-a-Judge prompting. (ii) Instruction following training : preference pairs are selected from the generated data,
which are used for training via DPO, resulting in model M t + 1 subscript 𝑀 𝑡 1 M_{t+1} . This whole procedure can then be iterated
resulting in both improved instruction following and reward modeling ability.

Figure 3 : Instruction following ability improves with Self-Training: We evaluate our models using head-to-head win rates on diverse prompts using GPT-4. The SFT Baseline is on par with Self-Rewarding Iteration 1 ( M 1 subscript 𝑀 1 M_{1} ).
However, Iteration 2 ( M 2 subscript 𝑀 2 M_{2} ) outperforms both Iteration 1 ( M 1 subscript 𝑀 1 M_{1} ) and the SFT Baseline.
Iteration 3 ( M 3 subscript 𝑀 3 M_{3} ) gives further gains over Iteration 2 ( M 2 subscript 𝑀 2 M_{2} ), outperforming M 1 subscript 𝑀 1 M_{1} , M 2 subscript 𝑀 2 M_{2} and the SFT Baseline by a large margin.

Figure 4 : AlpacaEval win rate breakdown for instruction categories (full names given in Appendix).
Self-Rewarding models give gains across several topics, but tend to e.g. give less gains on mathematics and reasoning tasks.

Figure 5 : Human evaluation results. Iterations of Self-Rewarding ( M 1 subscript 𝑀 1 M_{1} , M 2 subscript 𝑀 2 M_{2} and M 3 subscript 𝑀 3 M_{3} ) provide progressively better head-to-head win rates compared to the SFT baseline, in agreement with the automatic evaluation results.

Figure 8 : EFT data helps the self-rewarding loop: We evaluated the series of models trained using self-reward loops starting from the model trained using only IFT data. We performed head-to-head win rates comparisons on the IFT test set. While M 2 ′ superscript subscript 𝑀 2 ′ M_{2}^{\prime} can improve over the SFT baseline and M 3 ′ superscript subscript 𝑀 3 ′ M_{3}^{\prime} can improve even more over the SFT baseline, they lag far behind the corresponding models ( M 2 subscript 𝑀 2 M_{2} , M 3 subscript 𝑀 3 M_{3} ) that started from a base model trained using both IFT and EFT data, see Figure 3 .
